sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and usage notes
sections.what: Explains the purpose of the script, the rule that delay values are never recalculated, and the preview and execute modes. Imports the shared helper and its entry type.
sections.why: Gives the owner the purpose and the safe default before running it.
sections.watch_out: Keep the promise that delay values are not recalculated if the file is edited.

sections.name: entries (part 1)
sections.title: First group of LNG projects
sections.what: Lists the first group of LNG projects, from Adriatic through Gorgon, each with its stored delay and a note on how its dates were read.
sections.why: Each note explains the date reasoning, so the owner can check the judgment against the source.
sections.watch_out: The Angola LNG note describes about 18 months of delay while the stored value is 12, so the note and the number disagree on purpose.

sections.name: entries (part 2)
sections.title: Second group of LNG projects
sections.what: Lists the middle group of LNG projects, from Greater Tortue Ahmeyim through Pluto LNG Train 1, each with a stored delay and a note.
sections.why: Keeps each judgment next to its project data.
sections.watch_out: The two Pluto entries share the same note, so change both together if the note is ever corrected.

sections.name: entries (part 3)
sections.title: Last group of LNG projects
sections.what: Lists the last group of LNG projects, from Porto de Sergipe through Świnoujście, each with a stored delay and a note.
sections.why: Keeps the same pattern as the other groups so each row can be checked the same way.
sections.watch_out: Project names with special characters, such as Świnoujście, must match the database exactly for the helper to find them.

sections.name: entries (part 4)
sections.title: Running the LNG audit
sections.what: Passes the complete list to the shared helper under the LNG audit name. Any error is printed and the script exits with a failure code.
sections.why: Stops the run with a visible failure instead of hiding it.
sections.watch_out: The script runs as soon as the file is executed, so whether it previews or writes depends entirely on the flags given to the command.

summary: Marks LNG (liquefied natural gas) project delay values as approximate, because their planned or actual dates are only years or months, without changing the stored numbers.
purpose: Record that the existing schedule slip values for a long list of LNG projects rest on coarse dates, so the app does not present them as exact.
why: The header says current delay values are guarded and never recalculated, so the script only adds a flag and a note for each project.
how: The file holds a long hand-written list of LNG projects. Each entry has the stored delay, a note on how the dates were read, and the three fields checked. The list is handed to the shared helper markApproximateDelays under an audit name. Without the execute flag the helper only reports; with it, the helper writes. The helper's exact rules are not visible here.
inputs: A hard-coded list of LNG project IDs, names, stored delay values and notes, plus the database.
outputs: Approximate-delay marks in the database when run with the execute flag. Otherwise a preview, according to the header's run instructions.
risks: The list is long and typed by hand, so one mistyped ID or delay is easy to miss. For Angola LNG, the note says the source describes the delay as about 18 months, but the stored value is 12; the note says the stored value is kept and not recalculated, so the mismatch is known but unresolved.
debug: If one project fails, check its ID against the database. If a note seems wrong, compare it with the source text cited in the database evidence, since the code does not check the notes.
